header.stance: 勞動需求與實質殖利率轉強，油價下跌未能支撐美債

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 職缺與股市維持強勢，油價下跌未能支撐美債

美國職缺高於預期、科技股續漲，週二美債全線下跌，油價回落也未能扭轉賣壓。10年期殖利率上升6個基點至4.44%，升幅主要來自實質殖利率。相較週一長天期大致守穩，6月30日的跌勢已從2年期延伸到30年期。

數據讓Fed缺乏急於放鬆的理由。職缺增至759萬個、消費者信心改善，德州服務業的營收、招聘及售價也轉強。家庭對就業的看法轉弱、房價小跌，雖然使景氣並非一面倒向好，經濟活動與資產價格仍支持後續升息預期。原油下跌抑制通膨補償，卻擋不住實質殖利率回升。

海外債市並不同步。能源成本下降使歐洲央行更有餘裕觀望，日本長債卻因財政與通膨疑慮大跌，2年期標售的強勁需求也未擴及長端。信用市場整體資金充裕，日本企業及新興市場借款人的發債量都創紀錄；但Sable Offshore的高息貸款大幅縮減，顯示急迫還款與營運不確定性，仍足以讓個別借款人難以籌資。

## 勞動需求撐住，美債賣壓擴及中長天期

2年期美債殖利率上升4個基點至4.14%，5年期上升5個基點至4.19%，30年期也升5個基點至4.91%。10年期升幅較大，使2年與10年期利差擴大2個基點至30，2年與30年期擴大1個基點至77。長天期仍保有部分6月漲幅：整個月2年及5年期殖利率分別上升16、6個基點，10年及30年期則仍下降1、8個基點。

實質殖利率各天期同步上升。10年期增加4個基點至2.20%，損益兩平通膨率增加2個基點至2.24%。5年及7年期實質殖利率上升3、4個基點至1.93%、2.06%；20年及30年期各升5個基點至2.54%、2.73%。原油當日下跌，這次債券承壓主要反映實質資金成本提高，而非戰時能源衝擊重演。

5月職缺增至759萬個，高於預期及4月修正值。近期非農增幅回升後，這項資料顯示雇主的用人需求仍穩。6月美國經濟評議會消費者信心也小幅改善，但受訪者對就業情勢的評估惡化，對未來改善的期待有限。整體信心與就業細項並未同向轉強。

德州服務業則有較廣泛的改善。達拉斯Fed營收指數由5.0升至9.8，就業由−3.2升至8.1，一般企業活動由−7.7升至2.9；投入價格由29.7升至36.5，薪資福利由6.2升至15.3，售價由5.0升至7.7。房市相對疲弱，FHFA 4月房價指數月減0.1%，年增率降至2.0%。

即使油價已自戰時高點回落，市場仍預期Fed下半年至少升息一次。週二勞動與服務業資料支持這項判斷，房價及家庭就業觀感則提醒，不能把景氣視為全面加速。接下來的全國就業與製造業資料，將提供更完整的比較。

### 國庫券順利標售，交割集中在假日前

財政部標售$800億42天期國庫券，最高得標利率3.655%，投標倍數2.71。間接投標人取得競爭性得標額的69.01%，直接投標人4.96%，交易商26.03%；最高利率分配比例54.61%。發行與交割日均為7月2日。

次級市場6週期殖利率上升5個基點至3.73%，4週期卻下降2個基點至3.67%。8週期維持3.73%，13及17週期維持3.83%、3.88%；26及52週期各升1個基點至3.98%、3.97%。壓力集中於特定天期與資金日期，並非短期融資成本全面上漲。

錯誤交易另使DTCC罕見地在同一天進行兩輪交割，恰逢金融機構為季底申報縮減附買回交易。相關結算單位2025年底每日處理約$11.9兆交易，涵蓋政府債、公司債、市政債、股票與附買回。事件被描述為作業問題，尚非廣泛金融壓力；眼前重點是能否順利完成兩輪交割，避免延遲付款或被迫調度替換擔保品。

## 發債量創高，Sable卻付出高昂再融資代價

瑞穗金融與三井住友金融本週初合計定價近$100億美元債，使日本企業單季外幣發債達約$540億，年增逾80%。這是1999年有資料以來，首次單季超過$500億，Panasonic週二也啟動另一筆美元債。海外市場為收購與擴張提供較深的資金池；日圓貶值增加資金換回日圓後的金額，本地利率上升也改變了境內外融資的比較。

Sable Offshore即使提出15%固定利率，仍難完成原定再融資。槓桿貸款再度縮減，由最初$10億降至$6.75億，條件包括97美分價格、僅2.5年到期及期間攤還要求。公司另透過股票與可轉債籌措$4億，可轉債票息最高6.5%、轉換溢價30%至35%。股東面臨稀釋，股價一度大跌55%。

資金將用於償還原訂6月26日到期的Exxon Mobil定期貸款。Sable先前同意支付$3,000萬，將期限展至7月24日，目前預計再延至7月31日。JPMorgan負責股票與可轉債發行。加州外海業務雖已恢復部分營運，仍有訴訟風險，留給貸款人的評估時間短、現金流也不確定。其他槓桿借款人正縮減融資利差、加快成交，Sable卻在罕見高息下仍無法取得原定規模。

中國則限制另一類高成本再融資。國家發改委要求部分銀行避免承銷殖利率高於4%的境外人民幣債及高於5%的美元債，尤其針對地方政府融資平台。這類平台約有$1,170億境外債，中國企業在2026年剩餘期間約有$710億到期，2027年更逾$1,300億。部分額度削減10%至20%，已使至少一家國有借款人轉向較貴的短期銀行融資。

### 私募信貸重新募資，AI資產年限引發關注

規模$1.8兆的私募信貸市場面臨贖回增加，Len Tannenbaum卻正為新基金募資。他的家族擬投入最高$5,000萬，目標10月初完成首輪募集。他警告小型軟體公司未來一年可能難以再融資，但對EBITDA約$500萬至$2,500萬的企業放款較樂觀。既有投資人要求退出，對新貸款人而言，卻可能換來較高利差及較強契約保障。

IMF資本市場主管Tobias Adrian關注的是另一種期限風險：超大型雲端業者以中長期債務購置晶片及其他設備，資產卻可能在債務到期前很久就遭淘汰。他認為，強勁獲利及實際業績使這波熱潮有別於全面估值泡沫；債權人仍須判斷，設備創造的現金是否足以償還存續期間更長的負債。

公司債ETF當日以存續期間較長的投資級表現較弱。LQD跌0.57%，HYG及JNK僅跌0.05%、0.03%。股市上漲與波動率下降，伴隨高收益債基金相對有限的跌幅。

紐約收盤後，EchoStar旗下Dish聲請預先協商的破產重整。文件列出資產$10億至$100億、負債$100億至$500億。支持計畫的債權人持有超過88%的Dish DBS有擔保及無擔保債，並持有Dish Wireless逾$88億債務。方案擬提前償還$16億定期貸款與優先權益，並分配出售頻譜予AT&T所得的$202.5億。頻譜變現、爭議中的關係企業貸款及先前資產移轉，成為回收安排的核心。這是下一交易時段的新消息，並非週二基金報酬的原因。

## 歐洲通膨下降，日本長債卻大幅走弱

德國6月通膨由2.7%降至2.4%，低於預估2.5%；法國由2.8%降至2.0%，低於預估2.3%；義大利也降至3.1%，市場原以為持平。西班牙先前的3.6%則相對偏高。歐元區整體數據公布前，能源降價已反映在多個主要經濟體。

ECB 6月將政策利率升至2.25%，為2023年以來首次升息，官員隨後更傾向保留觀望空間。Martins Kazaks表示連續升息的急迫性大幅下降，Olli Rehn認為預期穩定、未見明顯第二輪效應。Philip Lane仍擔心過去四個月能源成本上升，接下來如何反映在食品與服務。分歧在於尚未完成的成本轉嫁，而非當下油價是否已下降。

德國勞動需求也沒有明顯升溫。季調失業人數只減少1,000人，BA-X需求指數維持103，最新估計的社會保險就業人數較一年前少7.1萬。

英國首季GDP成長確認為0.6%，服務業成長0.8%，但人均實質可支配所得下降0.8%。家庭儲蓄率由9.6%降至8.9%。基礎經常帳赤字縮小至£151億、占GDP 1.9%，初次所得改善抵銷了貿易逆差擴大。

英國央行總裁Andrew Bailey表示，油價下跌使政策重獲彈性。他認為戰前市場預期由3.75%降息兩次，原屬合理。原油已從逾$110跌至$80以下，也低於4月預測採用的路徑。他仍預期通膨今年稍後由2.8%升至約3.2%，但強調成長疲弱與中期展望，並未承諾即將降息。

日本30年期殖利率上升11個基點至3.94%，20年期上升9個基點至3.64%。首相高市早苗規劃截至2040會計年度動員逾¥370兆公私投資，引發融資與財政可持續性疑慮。日圓貶破162兌$1，進一步加深輸入通膨及日本央行正常化步調的爭論。

2年期需求卻很強。標售投標倍數由3.70升至4.82，高於過去12個月平均3.74，尾差由0.02縮至0.005，結果公布後殖利率下降1.5個基點。較高短端殖利率與央行逐步調整的預期吸引買盤，並未解決長端供給疑慮。

明治安田人壽計畫在截至2027年3月的會計年度買進逾¥2兆超長債，為原定規模兩倍，可能為長端提供新增需求。新任日本央行委員則表示通膨常態尚未穩固，支持審慎政策步調。紐約收盤後，IMF另建議紐西蘭央行在年底前，將2.25%利率提高至約3%的中性水準。

## 新興市場趁利差收窄籌資，各國政策仍有分歧

新興市場主權與企業上半年美元及歐元發債達創紀錄的$4,500億，年增15%，相對美債利差縮至154個基點、為2007年以來最窄。墨西哥、沙烏地阿拉伯、南韓、波蘭、土耳其與巴西各籌逾$100億。新興市場美元債報酬2.1%，為美債的三倍。週二美債殖利率上升，EMB回跌0.39%，但初級市場尚未出現資金撤離的跡象。

代表衣索比亞2024年到期債約45%持有人的委員會，確認已就主要重整條件達成初步協議，違約債週二倫敦早盤續漲至109.17美分。該國2023年12月漏付票息後，協議使談判向前推進；債權人仍批評IMF處理過程，以及同時擔任優先貸款人和債務可持續性評估者的角色。IMF回應，協議符合恢復債務可持續性的目標，並強調評估框架一致適用。

肯亞取得世界銀行批准的$7.5億發展政策貸款，與治理及公共財政改革連結，另一筆$5億永續連結聯貸也獲信用增強。擔保旨在降低成本、替換昂貴債務，財政與反貪腐改革仍是支持條件。

亞洲方面，印尼央行意外緊縮支撐印尼盾後，外資截至6月26日淨買進$12億政府債，為逾一年最強月度流入。10年期殖利率7.12%，低於6月稍早7.47%。

印度取消政府債稅負後，6月指數合格債外資增持達創紀錄的3,980億盧比、約$42億，高於週一報導的3,970億盧比。同月股市仍流出$31億。油價降低改善進口負擔，也有利盧比自5月接近97兌$1的低點回升，季風偏弱則可能推升食品價格。歐洲監理機關承認印度主權債結算機構資格，排除了德意志銀行與法國巴黎銀行等造市商的作業障礙，可望擴大外銀參與現券及衍生品市場。

哥倫比亞升息75個基點至12%，高於多數預估。此前法院已移除財長抵制出席即可癱瘓央行會議的規定。表決中四人支持升息、一人主張不變、兩人要求降息50個基點。5月通膨5.8%，受訪經濟學家預估年底約6.5%，遠高於3%目標及上下1個百分點容忍區間。央行恢復回應通膨的空間，債券與匯率均上漲。

其他市場則因通膨降溫走強。波蘭通膨由3.1%降至2.5%，低於預估2.7%，10年期殖利率降至3月初以來最低，茲羅提卻走弱。智利一年期損益兩平通膨率月降逾100個基點至2.19%。南非面臨相反壓力，兩年後通膨預期由3.6%升至3.9%，高於3%目標，遠期利率協議反映升息25個基點機率88%。

中國官方製造業PMI回到50.3，生產51.4、新訂單51.2，但就業48.5、小型企業48.2，仍低於榮枯線。非製造業維持50.2，營建49.0。產出及訂單改善尚未擴及小企業與就業，境外再融資收緊可能使這些較弱部門更難調度資金。

稍晚報導估計，委內瑞拉兩起地震造成$67億直接損失。投資人把災害支出納入原已艱難的重整評估，債券走低。這為下一交易時段增加財政與回收率問題，並非已完成美國盤的價格成因。

## 科技續漲，油價與波動率下滑

S&P 500上漲0.79%，Nasdaq 100上漲1.68%，半導體上漲3.92%，VIX下降6.80%至16.45。科技股強勁的單季行情延續至最後一天，股市仍有買盤，美債卻承受實質殖利率上升。

市場期待美伊達成持久協議，WTI跌1.77%至$69.50，布蘭特跌0.31%至$72.92，兩者月跌幅均逾20%。能源回落減輕歐洲通膨與原油進口國的負擔，美國勞動需求卻使美債未能從中取得足夠支撐。

美元指數僅升0.08%至101.19，仍比一個月前高2.31%。黃金近乎持平於$4,022.90，月跌11.79%。當日波動率下降、股市強勢與債券跌價並行，並非資金全面尋求避險。

對債券投資人，AI推動的股市行情還伴隨融資問題。強勁獲利支撐企業籌資，大量借款及部分設備較短的使用年限，卻使長期債權人承擔不同風險。這些疑慮不必等到科技股漲勢結束才值得關注。

## 非農與通膨公布後，市場即迎接假日

7月1日週三美東08:15公布ADP、09:45製造業PMI終值、10:00 ISM製造業與營建支出；因假日提前的非農及初領失業救濟金，週四08:30公布。招聘、薪資及工廠價格，將與較強的職缺及德州服務業資料相互對照。7月2日固定收益市場14:00收盤，數據公布後調整與融資的時間較短。

歐元區通膨初值7月1日中歐夏令11:00公布，前值為5月3.2%。德、法、義指向放緩，ECB仍須觀察服務物價與能源成本的延後轉嫁。油價及美伊停火也攸關後續走向；各國整體通膨下降，尚未解決Lane關注的食品與服務問題。

日本7月2日標售約¥2.6兆10年期債，7月7日再售約¥6,000億30年期。前一次2年期需求強勁、超長端卻重挫，這兩場標售可觀察更高殖利率能否吸引較長天期買盤，包括已提高購買計畫的壽險公司。

美國7月1日標售17週期國庫券，2日4及8週期各$850億。季底作業異常之後，新券交割、非農與提早收盤接踵而至。相較週二單一6週期殖利率上升，交易商承接及擔保融資利率，將更直接呈現實際資金移轉是否順暢。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Treasuries Fall as Jobs Data and Stocks Withstand Cheaper Oil

Treasuries fell across the curve Tuesday as stronger-than-expected job openings and a further rally in technology shares outweighed lower oil prices. The 10-year yield rose 6 basis points to 4.44%, with higher real yields accounting for most of the increase. Monday's losses had largely spared longer maturities; the June 30 selloff reached from two-year notes to the long bond.

The data gave the Fed little reason to hurry toward relief. Job openings increased to 7.59 million, consumer confidence improved, and Texas service businesses reported stronger revenue, hiring and prices. There were softer details—households were less confident about jobs and house prices slipped—but the combination of resilient activity and rising asset prices sustained expectations of further tightening. Falling crude restrained inflation compensation without preventing real yields from rising.

Overseas, the same decline in energy costs offered European central banks more room to wait. Japan's long bonds instead sold off sharply on fiscal and inflation concerns, despite strong demand for two-year debt. Credit financing remained plentiful overall: Japanese companies and emerging-market borrowers reported record issuance. Sable Offshore's costly, downsized loan showed how little that broad demand could help a borrower facing an urgent repayment and uncertain operations.

## Labor Demand Pushes the Selloff Beyond the Front End

The two-year Treasury yield rose 4 basis points to 4.14%, the five-year added 5 to 4.19%, and the 30-year increased 5 to 4.91%. The 10-year's larger rise steepened 2s10s by 2 basis points to 30; 2s30s widened 1 to 77. Longer maturities still retained some of June's gains. Over the month, two- and five-year yields were up 16 and 6 basis points, while 10- and 30-year yields remained down 1 and 8.

Real yields rose throughout the curve. The 10-year gained 4 basis points to 2.20%, and its breakeven inflation rate increased 2 to 2.24%. Five- and seven-year real yields rose 3 and 4 basis points to 1.93% and 2.06%; 20- and 30-year real yields each added 5, reaching 2.54% and 2.73%. With crude falling, renewed pressure on duration came mainly from real borrowing costs rather than a return to the wartime energy shock.

May job openings rose to 7.59 million, above expectations and April's revised level. Coming after the recent pickup in payroll growth, the release suggested employers' demand for workers was holding up. June Conference Board confidence also edged higher, although consumers assessed employment conditions less favorably and expected little improvement. Aggregate confidence and the labor-market detail were pointing in different directions.

Texas services strengthened more broadly. The Dallas Fed revenue index rose to 9.8 from 5.0, employment to 8.1 from −3.2 and general business activity to 2.9 from −7.7. Input prices increased to 36.5 from 29.7, wages and benefits to 15.3 from 6.2, and selling prices to 7.7 from 5.0. Housing offered a softer offset: the FHFA price index fell 0.1% in April, slowing annual appreciation to 2.0%.

Expectations of at least one Fed increase in the second half had survived oil's retreat from its wartime peak. Tuesday's labor and services reports supported that view, even if weaker housing and household job perceptions argued against treating the economy as uniformly strong. The next national employment and manufacturing releases would show whether the regional strength extended further.

### Bills Clear Ahead of a Crowded Settlement Day

Treasury sold $80 billion of 42-day bills at a 3.655% high rate and 2.71 bid-to-cover ratio. Indirect bidders took 69.01% of accepted competitive tenders, direct bidders 4.96% and dealers 26.03%; the allotment at the high was 54.61%. The securities issue and settle July 2.

Secondary six-week bill yields rose 5 basis points to 3.73%, while four-week yields fell 2 to 3.67%. Eight-week bills held at 3.73%; 13- and 17-week yields were unchanged at 3.83% and 3.88%. The 26- and 52-week maturities each added 1 basis point to 3.98% and 3.97%. Pressure was concentrated around particular maturities and cash dates rather than a uniform rise in short-term funding costs.

Erroneous trades also forced a rare double-settlement day at DTCC just as firms were reducing repo activity for quarter-end reporting. The affected clearing unit handled about $11.9 trillion daily at the end of 2025 across markets including government, corporate and municipal debt, equities and repo. The incident was described as an operational snag, not evidence of broad financial stress. Its immediate importance was whether both settlement cycles could be completed without payment delays or disruptive collateral substitutions.

## Record Issuance Meets a Costly Refinancing at Sable

Mizuho Financial Group and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group priced almost $10 billion of dollar debt at the start of the week, taking Japanese companies' quarterly foreign-currency issuance to about $54 billion. Sales were more than 80% above a year earlier and exceeded $50 billion in a quarter for the first time in data back to 1999. Panasonic began another dollar offering Tuesday. Overseas markets offered depth for acquisitions and expansion, while the weak yen increased the domestic proceeds available when funds were swapped back and higher local rates changed the funding comparison.

Sable Offshore struggled to refinance even with a 15% fixed coupon. Its proposed leveraged loan was cut again, from an original $1 billion to $675 million, despite a 97-cent offer price, a short 2.5-year maturity and amortization requirements. It also sought $400 million from stock and convertible notes. The converts offered a coupon of up to 6.5% and a 30%–35% conversion premium; shares fell as much as 55% as investors confronted the dilution.

The proceeds were intended to repay an Exxon Mobil term loan originally due June 26. Sable had agreed to pay $30 million to extend it to July 24, and the extension was now expected to run through July 31. JPMorgan was running the stock and note offering. Restarted California offshore operations remained exposed to litigation, leaving lenders little time and uncertain cash flow to assess. Other leveraged borrowers were tightening terms and accelerating deals, but Sable could not obtain its original loan size on unusually expensive terms.

China was restricting a different form of costly refinancing. The National Development and Reform Commission asked selected bankers not to underwrite offshore yuan bonds yielding above 4% or dollar bonds above 5%, particularly for local-government financing vehicles. LGFVs had about $117 billion of offshore debt outstanding. Chinese companies faced roughly $71 billion of maturities in the remainder of 2026 and more than $130 billion in 2027. Quotas had been cut 10%–20% in some cases, pushing at least one state-owned borrower toward more expensive short-term bank funding.

### Private Credit and the Useful Life of AI Assets

Len Tannenbaum was seeking money for a new fund as redemption requests rose at major alternative managers in the $1.8 trillion private-credit market. His family planned to supply up to $50 million, with an initial close targeted for early October. He warned that smaller software companies could struggle to refinance within a year, while describing lending to businesses with roughly $5 million–$25 million of EBITDA more favorably. Wider spreads and stronger covenants could benefit new lenders, even as existing investors sought liquidity.

IMF capital-markets director Tobias Adrian raised a separate concern about AI financing: hyperscalers were issuing medium- and long-term debt for chips and other physical assets that could become obsolete much sooner. Strong profits and earnings delivery distinguished the boom from a generalized valuation bubble in his assessment. Creditors still had to judge whether the cash generated by those assets would cover debt outstanding long after the technology had changed.

Listed funds reflected Tuesday's higher Treasury yields more heavily in investment-grade duration. LQD fell 0.57%, while HYG and JNK slipped only 0.05% and 0.03%. Rising stocks and lower volatility accompanied the relatively small high-yield losses.

After the New York close, EchoStar's Dish unit filed a prepackaged bankruptcy. Filings listed $1 billion–$10 billion of assets and $10 billion–$50 billion of liabilities. Holders of more than 88% of Dish DBS secured and unsecured notes, also holding over $8.8 billion of Dish Wireless debt, supported the plan. It envisaged early repayment of $1.6 billion in term loans and preferred interests and distribution of proceeds from a $20.25 billion spectrum sale to AT&T. Spectrum monetization, disputed intercompany lending and earlier asset transfers now became central to the recovery process. This was a fresh development for the next session, not a cause of Tuesday's fund returns.

## European Inflation Eases as Japan's Long Bonds Sell Off

German June inflation slowed to 2.4% from 2.7%, below the 2.5% forecast. France fell to 2.0% from 2.8%, versus an expected 2.3%, and Italy eased to 3.1% when economists had anticipated no change. Spain's previously reported 3.6% stood apart. Lower energy prices were showing through in several major economies ahead of the euro-area release.

ECB officials increasingly saw room to wait after June's first increase since 2023 took the policy rate to 2.25%. Martins Kazaks said the urgency of consecutive moves had fallen significantly; Olli Rehn saw anchored expectations and no major second-round effects. Philip Lane remained concerned about how four months of higher energy costs could feed into food and services. The disagreement was about the remaining pass-through, rather than whether current oil prices had fallen.

German labor demand offered little sign of renewed pressure. Seasonally adjusted unemployment fell by only 1,000, the BA-X demand index held at 103 and the latest estimate showed social-insurance employment 71,000 below a year earlier.

Britain's first-quarter GDP growth was confirmed at 0.6%, supported by 0.8% services growth, but real disposable income per person fell 0.8%. Households reduced their saving ratio to 8.9% from 9.6%. The underlying current-account deficit narrowed to £15.1 billion, or 1.9% of GDP, as an improvement in primary income outweighed a wider trade deficit.

BOE Governor Andrew Bailey said lower oil had restored policy flexibility. Before the war, market pricing for two cuts from the 3.75% rate had been reasonable, in his view. Crude was now below $80 after exceeding $110 and below the path assumed in April's forecast. Bailey still expected inflation to rise from 2.8% to about 3.2% later in the year, but emphasized weak growth and the medium-term outlook rather than committing to an imminent cut.

Japan's 30-year yield rose 11 basis points to 3.94%, and the 20-year added 9 to 3.64%. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's plan for more than ¥370 trillion of public and private investment through fiscal 2040 increased concern about financing and fiscal sustainability. The yen's fall beyond 162 per dollar compounded imported-inflation concerns and doubts about how quickly the BOJ would be able to normalize policy.

Two-year debt found much stronger demand. The auction's bid-to-cover ratio climbed to 4.82 from 3.70, above the 3.74 average over 12 months, and the tail narrowed to 0.005 from 0.02. The two-year yield fell 1.5 basis points after the sale. Elevated short yields and expectations of gradual BOJ moves attracted buyers without resolving the long end's supply concerns.

Meiji Yasuda offered a potential source of longer-duration demand, planning more than ¥2 trillion of super-long purchases in the fiscal year ending March 2027—twice its earlier plan. A newly appointed BOJ board member said an inflationary norm was not yet firmly established, also favoring a cautious policy outlook. Later, after New York closed, the IMF urged New Zealand's central bank to raise its 2.25% rate toward a neutral level centered near 3% by year-end.

## Emerging Borrowers Secure Funding as Local Policies Diverge

Emerging-market sovereigns and companies sold a record $450 billion of dollar and euro bonds in the first half, up 15% from a year earlier. Spreads over Treasuries narrowed to 154 basis points, the tightest since 2007. Mexico, Saudi Arabia, South Korea, Poland, Turkey and Brazil each raised more than $10 billion. EM dollar debt returned 2.1%, three times the Treasury gain. Tuesday brought a reversal in broad fund performance—EMB fell 0.39% as US yields rose—but little evidence that the primary market had closed.

Ethiopia's creditor committee, representing about 45% of its 2024 notes, confirmed a tentative agreement on key restructuring terms. Defaulted bonds extended their gains to 109.17 cents Tuesday morning in London. The country had missed a coupon in December 2023. The agreement advanced the negotiations, though creditors criticized the IMF's handling of the process and its roles as senior lender and debt-sustainability assessor. The IMF said the agreement was consistent with restoring sustainability and defended the consistent application of its framework.

Kenya secured World Bank approval for a $750 million development-policy loan tied to governance and public-finance reforms, plus an enhancement to a separate $500 million sustainability-linked syndicated loan. The guarantee was intended to reduce borrowing costs and replace expensive debt. Continued fiscal and anti-corruption reforms remained part of that support.

In Asia, foreign investors bought a net $1.2 billion of Indonesian government bonds through June 26, the strongest monthly pace in more than a year, after Bank Indonesia's unexpected tightening to support the rupiah. The 10-year yield was 7.12%, down from 7.47% earlier in June.

India's June purchases reached a record 398 billion rupees, about $4.2 billion, in index-eligible government bonds after the removal of taxes on government debt. The rupee total was up from 397 billion reported Monday. Foreigners still withdrew $3.1 billion from equities. Lower oil helped the import bill and the rupee's recovery from May's low near 97 per dollar, while a weak monsoon threatened food prices. European regulators' recognition of India's sovereign-bond clearinghouse removed an operational obstacle for market makers including Deutsche Bank and BNP Paribas, potentially widening foreign-bank participation in cash bonds and derivatives.

Colombia raised its policy rate 75 basis points to 12%, more than most forecasts, after a court removed the government's ability to paralyze central-bank meetings through a finance-minister boycott. Four board members backed the increase, one favored no change and two sought a half-point cut. May inflation was 5.8%, with surveyed economists expecting about 6.5% by year-end against a 3% target with a one-point tolerance band. Bonds and the currency rallied as the decision restored scope to respond to inflation.

Other local markets moved on disinflation. Poland's inflation fell to 2.5% from 3.1%, below the 2.7% forecast, taking its 10-year yield to the lowest since early March even as the zloty weakened. Chile's one-year breakeven had fallen more than 100 basis points during the month to 2.19%. South Africa faced the opposite pressure: two-year-ahead expectations rose to 3.9% from 3.6%, above its 3% target, and forward-rate agreements priced an 88% chance of a quarter-point increase.

China's official manufacturing PMI returned to expansion at 50.3, with production at 51.4 and new orders at 51.2. Employment remained below 50 at 48.5, as did the small-firm index at 48.2. Non-manufacturing activity held at 50.2 and construction at 49.0. The improvement in output and orders had yet to extend to smaller firms and employment, where tighter offshore refinancing could be more difficult to absorb.

A later report put the direct damage from twin Venezuelan earthquakes at $6.7 billion. Bonds were falling as investors considered disaster spending alongside an already difficult restructuring. The news added a fiscal and creditor-recovery problem for the next session, rather than explaining the completed US close.

## Technology Rallies While Oil and Volatility Fall

The S&P 500 rose 0.79%, Nasdaq 100 gained 1.68% and semiconductors advanced 3.92%. VIX fell 6.80% to 16.45. Technology's strong quarter continued into its final day, supporting equity valuations while the Treasury market absorbed higher real yields.

WTI fell 1.77% to $69.50 and Brent eased 0.31% to $72.92 on hopes for a durable US-Iran settlement. Both were down more than 20% over the month. The decline eased the energy burden on European inflation and oil importers, but Treasury yields rose nonetheless as US labor demand held up.

DXY rose just 0.08% to 101.19, still 2.31% above a month earlier. Gold was nearly unchanged at $4,022.90 after an 11.79% monthly decline. The day's falling volatility and strong equities contrasted with losses in duration, rather than signaling a broad search for protection.

For bond investors, AI's contribution to the equity rally also carried a financing question. Strong earnings supported access to capital, while the large borrowing requirements and short useful life of some equipment left a different set of risks for long-term creditors. Those concerns could persist without ending the rally in technology shares.

## Payrolls and Inflation Arrive Before the Holiday

Wednesday, July 1 brings ADP at 08:15 ET, final manufacturing PMI at 09:45, and ISM manufacturing and construction spending at 10:00. The holiday-advanced payroll report and initial claims follow Thursday at 08:30. Hiring, wages and factory prices will give a national comparison for the stronger JOLTS and Texas services reports. The July 2 fixed-income session ends at 14:00, leaving less time to trade and fund positions after the releases.

Euro-area flash inflation is due July 1 at 11:00 CEST after May's 3.2% headline rate. Germany, France and Italy point toward a slowdown, with services and the delayed effect of higher energy costs still important to the ECB. Oil and the US-Iran ceasefire remain relevant to that outlook; national headline declines alone do not settle the food and services question raised by Lane.

Japan sells roughly ¥2.6 trillion of new 10-year bonds July 2 and about ¥600 billion of 30-year debt July 7. These auctions follow the strong two-year sale and sharp super-long losses. End-investor participation will show whether higher yields can attract demand farther out the curve, including insurers increasing purchase plans.

US 17-week bills are scheduled July 1, followed by $85 billion each of four- and eight-week bills July 2. New bill settlement, payrolls and the early close coincide after the quarter-end processing disruption. Dealer allotments and secured funding rates should provide a clearer picture of the cash transfer than Tuesday's isolated six-week yield increase alone.
